subject: Renewal proposal: 24-month staged capacity + auto-upgrade triggers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T16:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal proposal: 24-month staged capacity + auto-upgrade triggers

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call earlier today. Attached is a sketch of a renewal structure that would move BrightMaps from an annual renewal to a 24-month agreement with graduated capacity tiers and an automated upgrade mechanism to keep your apps performant as usage grows.

Quick summary:
- Term: 24 months, with option to co-term to BrightMaps fiscal year (July 1) at the next fiscal boundary.
- Capacity: Staged unlocks (Q1 baseline, +25% each quarter up to 2x baseline).
- Auto-upgrade trigger: automatic promotion to the next tier if sustained utilization >= 70% for a rolling 30-day window; each promotion includes a 10-business-day opt-out window to pause the upgrade.
- Billing: Quarterly invoicing by default; annual prepay option available for a 6% discount.
- Safeguard: 60-day trial of the first upgraded tier where we provide a 50% credit for any SLA shortfalls.

Attachments: BrightMaps_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf, Ramp_Schedule_CSV.csv

Can you confirm whether procurement/finance will accept quarterly billing, and whether an auto-upgrade tied to utilization is acceptable (or if you need manual approvals)? If quarterly billing is a blocker, we can propose a yearly invoice cadence with a smaller prepay and slightly different discounting.

Looping in Karthik to confirm flexibility on pricing ramps.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Marissa —

Thanks for sending this over. A few quick points from procurement/finance:
1) Billing cadence: Finance prefers annual invoices tied to our FY but will consider quarterly if Redwood can provide an annual PO and invoice schedule.
2) Auto-upgrade: We like the idea of automated scaling but need a hard cap and an option to require manual sign-off above 1.5x baseline. Automatic upgrades to >1.5x would need executive approval.
3) Exit/notice: For a 24-month term we need a 90-day early-exit clause with a defined buyout that scales down over the first 12 months.

Diego (cc'd) handles procurement ops and will share our standard amendment template. Can you include a version that co-terms to our FY and a variant that stays calendar-year co-term?

Thanks,
Lina

BrightMaps Inc.

Thanks for sharing. A couple of product/pricing suggestions before we send a revised doc to Lina:

- Make the opt-out window explicit (10 business days) and allow them one pre-authorized override per 12 months for emergency scaling.

Hi Lina and Diego —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached are two formal options:
1) Co-term to BrightMaps FY (July 1): 24-month term with staged unlocks and auto-upgrade up to 150% without exec approval; >150% requires executive sign-off. Annual invoicing variant included.
2) Calendar-year co-term: identical staging but with quarterly billing by default.

We also added a buyout schedule for early exit (90-day notice with buyout equal to remaining committed value prorated to 75% in months 1–6, 50% months 7–12, 25% months 13–18, 0% after month 18).

Attachments: RDW_Amendment_Draft.docx (amendment draft), BrightMaps_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (updated)

Could you confirm which billing cadence your finance team will accept and whether the manual approval threshold >150% is workable? If both are acceptable we'll produce a final amendment for legal to redline.
